items.criterion: The checker module declares the exact session schema identifier the instrument reads, and the chain it publishes has one entry for every zero-reason the compiled test table names, so the instrument and the table cannot disagree about how many checkers exist.

Every checker published in the chain declares a zero-reason and every declared zero-reason belongs to a published checker, as set equality in both directions, so no checker can fire without a reason and no reason can exist without a checker.
items.evaluation_target: tests/checkers.py::CHAIN names versus the REASONS table
items.judgment: set_equality({name for name, _ in checkers.CHAIN}, set(REASONS))

items.criterion: No two checkers share a zero-reason, and every reason the table uses is a published upper-case string constant of the checker module, so a zero score always resolves to exactly one identifiable cause.

Each chain entry names a check_ function that is actually defined in the checker module source, and the callable the chain carries is that same module attribute rather than an unrelated object bound under the same name.
items.evaluation_target: tests/checkers.py function definitions versus CHAIN entries

items.criterion: The grader imports exactly the check_ functions the chain publishes and imports nothing else from the checker module, so no ungraded helper can reach the grading path.
items.evaluation_target: tests/grade.py import statements from the checkers module

items.criterion: The checker module imports no member of the forbidden set and imports nothing outside the allowlist, so no checker can read a clock, a random source, the network, the operating system or a tensor library.
The grader never imports the agent submission and never reaches it through dynamic import machinery, so submitted code cannot execute inside the grading process.
items.judgment: absent("import refine", grade.py) and absent("importlib", grade.py)

items.criterion: The recipe schema names the frozen capacity axes and exposes none of them as a writable field, so a submission cannot widen the model or spend more tokens through the same surface it uses to tune free axes.
The abort floor in the test harness writes exactly the set of score documents the score module names, so an aborted run leaves no score document missing and invents none.
items.evaluation_target: tests/test.sh printf literals versus tests/score.py document names

items.criterion: No abort-floor JSON literal repeats a key, so no reader can silently take a different value than another reader depending on which duplicate its parser keeps.

The abort floor emits the same score.json and score_full.json document, carries the same key set the grader writes for the same inputs, is byte-equal to what the score module emits, and writes the bare score as 0.000000, so the aborted path and the graded path cannot diverge in what a downstream reader sees.
items.evaluation_target: tests/test.sh abort-floor documents versus tests/score.py write output
items.judgment: equality(floor[SCORE_DOC], floor[SCORE_FULL]) and for_each(floor, set_equality(keys(floor[name]), keys(graded[name]))) and equality(floor[SCORE_FULL], graded[SCORE_FULL]) and equality(bare, "0.000000\n")
